proposals.before: Jianye has long been called the abode of emperors; its rivers and mountains are majestic and its terrain broad, and the Six Dynasties in succession made it their capital.
proposals.after: Jiankang has long been called the abode of emperors; its rivers and mountains are majestic and its terrain broad, and the Six Dynasties in succession made it their capital.
proposals.reason: Chinese 建康 is Jiankang; rendering it as Jianye (建業), an earlier name, mismatches the source graph and later units that correctly use Jiankang.

proposals.before: Your minister once surveyed the strategic geography of the whole realm and ranked Guanzhong first; speaking now of the southeast alone, Jianye is the better choice.
proposals.after: Your minister once surveyed the strategic geography of the whole realm and ranked Guanzhong first; speaking now of the southeast alone, Jiankang is the better choice.
proposals.reason: Same 建康→Jianye mismatch as s0053.

proposals.before: Since the imperial carriage has not yet returned to the old capital, it would be best to halt temporarily at Jianye as an expedient measure.
proposals.after: Since the imperial carriage has not yet returned to the old capital, it would be best to halt temporarily at Jiankang as an expedient measure.
proposals.reason: Same 建康→Jianye mismatch as s0053.

proposals.before: Your subject wishes Your Majesty to command the chief ministers to join hearts and combine strength, exert all human effort and then await Heaven's decree — then recovering territory, cutting down whales and crocodiles, and welcoming back the two palaces will surely come to pass in time.
proposals.after: Your subject wishes Your Majesty to command the chief ministers to join hearts and combine strength, exert all human effort and then await Heaven's decree — then recovering territory, cutting down whales and crocodiles, and welcoming back the Two Sovereigns will surely come to pass in time.
proposals.reason: 兩宮 here denotes the two captive emperors (parallel to idiomatic Two Sovereigns), not architectural palaces.

decisions.reason: Source 建康 is Jiankang; idiomatic Jianye (建業) substitutes an earlier toponym for a different graph, and Jiankang restores the place-name as written.
則當以建康為便 names Jiankang as the preferred southeast seat; idiomatic Jianye mismatches that graph and the same place named 建康 in the flanking units.
且于建康權宜駐蹕 specifies a temporary halt at Jiankang; rendering the site as Jianye invents the wrong toponym against the Chinese.

迎還兩宮 in this memorial means welcoming back the two captive emperors, as the unit’s idiomatic Two Sovereigns already renders; lowercase two palaces wrongly suggests buildings, and Two Sovereigns restores the persons meant.
